content: 1. Antacids should be administered at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours after taking the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine. For rilpivirine alone, antacids should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after administration to avoid significant decreases in rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. 2. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. However, rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 3. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with antiretroviral medications (ARTs) for at least one month before cell mobilization or until the expected duration for elimination of the medications. ARTs may interfere with the manufacturing of autologous cell therapies such as atidarsagene autotemcel. 4. Both atomoxetine and rilpivirine increase the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring. Similarly, rilpivirine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised when rilpivirine is co-administered with drugs known to increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 5. Co-administration of rilpivirine with bedaquiline, betibeglogene autotemcel, or buprenorphine (in various formulations) is associated with an increased QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be considered, and co-administration should be avoided if possible. 6. Calcium-containing compounds (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, or calcium/vitamin D) decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. If co-administration is necessary, these agents should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Close monitoring and therapy modification may be required. 7. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which may result in a loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or other NNRTIs. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be used to avoid potential risks. 9. Chloroquine increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Although the significance is unknown, caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of chlorpromazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised when co-administering rilpivirine with drugs that increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 11. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH, which may lead to treatment failure or resistance. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 12. Ciprofloxacin, citalopram, and clarithromycin increase rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required when co-administering rilpivirine with these drugs. 13. Clozapine and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Conivaptan and crizotinib increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. Crizotinib also increases the QTc interval, though the clinical significance is unknown. 15. Cyclobenzaprine, dasatinib, and degarelix increase rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Desflurane and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be considered. 17. Desipramine and deutetrabenazine increase rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Although deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent at recommended doses, caution and close monitoring are still advised. 18. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the potential for virologic failure and resistance. 19. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure or resistance. 20. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal. No dose adjustment is required when rilpivirine is co-administered with didanosine. 21. Disopyramide, dofetilide, and dolasetron increase rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with dofetilide should be avoided. 22. Donepezil, doxepin, and dronedarone increase the QTc interval when co-administered with rilpivirine. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Droperidol and efavirenz increase rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration with efavirenz is contraindicated. 24. Eliglustat and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 25. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be co-administered with rilpivirine or other antiretrovirals. 26. Encorafenib, entrectinib, and eribulin increase the QTc interval when co-administered with rilpivirine. Alternative drugs should be considered. 27. Erythromycin (in various formulations) increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Escitalopram increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Esomeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to treatment failure or resistance. 31. Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 33. Fexinidazole and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 34. Fingolimod and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Flecainide increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 36. Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. No dose adjustment is required, but caution and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Fluoxetine increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 38. Foscarnet increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Fosphenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Fostemsavir and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 41. Gemifloxacin increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 42. Gepirone and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Gilteritinib and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 44. Givinostat and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 45. Granisetron increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 46. Haloperidol increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 47. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 48. Hydroxyzine and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Famotidine should be administered at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. 50. Ibutinide increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 51. Iloperidone increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 52. Indapamide increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Indinavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are required. 54. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 55. Isoniazid increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 56. Isradipine increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 57. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. No dose adjustment is required, but caution and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Ketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but caution and close monitoring are advised. 59. Lansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated. 60. Lapatinib increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Lefamulin and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 62. Levofloxacin increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 63. Levoketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but caution and close monitoring are recommended. 64. Lithium and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are required. 65. Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 66. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing may be interfered with by ARTs. ARTs should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 67. Lumefantrine increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 68. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both increase the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided. 69. Magnesium-containing compounds (e.g., magnesium chloride, magnesium gluconate) decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. If co-administration is necessary, these agents should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Close monitoring and therapy modification may be required.
